none_means: No qualifying prior reference verified; not a proof of novelty.

results.references: - Nikita Kornilov, Alexander Gasnikov, Pavel Dvurechensky, Darina Dvinskikh. [Gradient-Free Methods for Non-Smooth Convex Stochastic Optimization with Heavy-Tailed Noise on Convex Compact](https://arxiv.org/html/2304.02442v3). 2023 (preprint v3, August 24). Complexity: $O(1+dM_2^2D^2/\varepsilon^2)$ paired stochastic function-value calls for $\mathbb E[f(\bar x)-f(x^*)]\le\varepsilon$, using Euclidean ZO-RSMD with moment exponent $2$; here $M_2$ bounds the RMS sample Lipschitz constant, $0<\varepsilon\le M_2D$, smoothing radius $\tau=\Theta(\varepsilon/M_2)\le\gamma_{\max}$, and $\Delta\le c\varepsilon^2/(\sqrt d M_2D)$ for a sufficiently small universal $c$. Each pair comprises two scalar evaluations; the budget is fixed.

problem_class.label: convex
problem_class.details: Minimize f over a compact convex Q ⊂ ℝ^d of diameter at most D, with x0 and a minimizer xstar in Q. On Q + closedBall(0, γmax), f is convex and M-Lipschitz. When smooth=true, its gradient is L-Lipschitz on the interior; otherwise nonsmooth objectives are permitted.

oracle.label: function_value
oracle.details: A scalar query at x returns F(x,w)+δ(x), with E[F(x,w)]=f(x). Calls 2k and 2k+1 share the same sample ξk; different pairs use independent identically distributed samples. Neither samples nor gradients are returned. The extracted budget counts 6T+4N individual scalar evaluations.
oracle.evidence: LongTails/Setups/AdaptivePairedZerothOrder.lean: spec.Query, spec.Reply, spec.admissible, oracle law ξ(n/2); LongTails/Setups/StochasticGeneralizedSmoothAndConvex.lean: IID; supplied extracted budget; LongTails/Template.lean: execute.

distinctive_assumptions.label: unknown_smoothness
distinctive_assumptions.details: The algorithm receives d, Q, x0, project, D, γmax, ε, ell, N and T. The smoothness flag and M, M2, L, Δ are hidden. Public horizons must satisfy T ≥ 2^48(d+ell)(1+M2²D²/ε²)+N. The smooth branch requires N ≥ 32(1+√(LD²/ε)); the nonsmooth branch requires N ≥ 1024(1+d^(1/4)MD/ε+d^(1/4)D√(M/(γmax ε))).
distinctive_assumptions.evidence: LongTails/Setups/AdaptivePairedZerothOrder.lean: Public, Params, spec.publicInput, spec.valid; LongTails/Template.lean: Convergence.makeAlgorithm.

distinctive_assumptions.label: heavy_tailed_noise
distinctive_assumptions.details: Sample weak gradients may have heavy tails with finite second moment; exponential moments, bounded realizations, and moments above order two are not required.

distinctive_assumptions.label: bounded_variance
distinctive_assumptions.details: The actual moment condition is the uncentered bound E‖G(x,w)‖²≤M2² at every interior point. G is a weak gradient of the sample function, not an observed oracle reply. No second-moment bound on function values is imposed.
distinctive_assumptions.evidence: LongTails/Setups/AdaptivePairedZerothOrder.lean: spec.admissible, final integrability and squared-norm integral conditions.

distinctive_assumptions.label: biased_oracle
distinctive_assumptions.details: A fixed measurable perturbation δ satisfies |δ(x)|≤Δ on the enlarged domain. With r=min(γmax,D/N) in the smooth branch and r=min(γmax,d^(1/4)D/N) otherwise, √d Δ/r ≤ ε/(16384D). No continuity or Lipschitz condition is imposed on δ.

distinctive_assumptions.label: finite_dimensional
distinctive_assumptions.details: The ambient space is Euclidean ℝ^d with d>0. An exact Euclidean projection onto Q is publicly available.

distinctive_assumptions.label: other
distinctive_assumptions.details: Almost every sample function is continuous on the enlarged domain and admits a locally integrable distributional gradient G there, expressed through integration by parts against smooth compactly supported test functions. Samplewise convexity and a square-integrable global sample Lipschitz constant are not assumed. Dependence is confined to the prescribed adjacent query pairs.
distinctive_assumptions.evidence: LongTails/Setups/AdaptivePairedZerothOrder.lean: spec.admissible, sample continuity, weak-gradient identity, and oracle law.

accuracy.label: objective_gap
accuracy.details: The target is f(output)−f(xstar)≤ε, with ε>0. Both the output and its objective gap must be measurable.

accuracy.label: feasibility
accuracy.details: The output belongs to Q for every seed, including seeds in the objective-error failure event.

accuracy.label: high_probability
accuracy.details: P(f(output)−f(xstar)>ε)≤8 exp(−ell), with ell≥log 8. Probability includes both algorithm randomization and the paired oracle samples; the oracle budget is fixed.

setup_category.label: non_standard
setup_category.reason: This combines paired stochastic function evaluations, deterministic bounded bias, pointwise second moments of distributional sample gradients, hidden regularity parameters, and a fixed-budget confidence guarantee. These features go beyond the usual stochastic zeroth-order benchmark. Implementation and proofs were not inspected; the literature comparison does not establish novelty.
